sn6.11:1.2: The Serpentine (_sappinī_) is probably the modern Panchane (from _pañcānana_, “five-mouthed”). There was a wanderer’s hermitage on its banks ([an3.64](), [an4.30](), [an4.185]()).
sn6.11:1.3: Sanaṅkumāra (“Everyoung”) became a Hindu deity closely associated with the worship of Krishna. He first appears in the seventh chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad. He speaks this verse also at [dn3:1.28.2](), [dn27:32.2](), [mn53:25.3](), [an11.10:6.1](), and it was endorsed by the Buddha. He features in two extended discussions among the gods, his appearance heralded by a great light in the north ([dn18:15.1](), [dn19:15.1]()). He also appears in [dn20:20.3]().
